summary: The paper proposes a Toeplitz-matrix unification of positional encodings (additive vs. multiplicative) and uses two controlled synthetic tasks to identify a 'single-head deposit pattern' in RoPE, supported by head-wise causal ablations, several targeted follow-up ablations, and an MLA hybrid that diffuses the pattern. The core empirical observation is interesting and the experimental logic is mostly sound, but the theoretical section largely assumes its conclusion (gain factors asserted > 1, an existential 'there exists a batch' cancellation claim, and a single-kernel Hadamard form of RoPE that glosses over per-frequency rotations), and all evidence is confined to two toy tasks at one model scale. The framing repeatedly overreaches the evidence (e.g., the deposit pattern as the 'primary cause' of RoPE's practical gap, which the authors themselves admit is unvalidated). This is a promising borderline submission that needs substantial theoretical tightening and broader empirical validation.
strengths: A clean, well-motivated controlled experimental design: the position-sensitive vs. position-agnostic task pair cleanly isolates content-position coupling, and the six-PE comparison with 5 seeds is a reasonable empirical backbone.

The single-head deposit pattern is a crisp, falsifiable mechanistic observation, and the head-wise causal ablation (Figure 4) plus the Absolute-PE injection, RoPE-subset, and p_i-removal ablations form a coherent causal argument that it stems from RoPE's multiplicative structure.
The MLA experiment (Table 1, Figure 7) connects the diagnosis to an actionable architectural remedy, showing the analysis can predict and mitigate the pathology rather than only describe it.

The paper is honestly structured with an explicit Limitations section acknowledging the unvalidated link to length extrapolation, and the figure/table captions describe display items that directly support the claims.

key_concerns.issue: The theoretical analysis is not sound as stated: Theorem 6.1's 'exponential amplification' simply posits gain factors gamma_k > 1 (assuming the conclusion), Proposition 6.2 proves only that *there exists* a batch making ALiBi's gradient vanish (an existential statement that says little about training in practice), and Eq. (2) collapses RoPE's per-frequency-pair rotations into a single Toeplitz kernel Ge via one Hadamard product, which is not obviously exact.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Derive the gain factors from the RoPE kernel's spectrum rather than assuming them, restate Proposition 6.2 as a typical-case (in-expectation or high-probability) result, and either prove Eq. (2) exactly as a sum of per-frequency Toeplitz kernels or clearly scope it as an approximation with error bounds.

key_concerns.issue: Generality is under-supported: all evidence comes from two synthetic tasks, one 6-layer decoder, one scale, and no real-language or length-extrapolation evaluation, while the title and introduction frame the work as explaining RoPE's general 'performance paradox'.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add at least one experiment on real language data or a length-extrapolation benchmark (even small-scale), and replicate the deposit pattern across depths/widths to show it is not an artifact of one configuration.

key_concerns.issue: The claim that the deposit pattern is 'unique to RoPE' is evidenced in the main text only against NoPE on Task 1 and RoPE on Task 2; comparable head-ablation violins for the additive PEs (Absolute, T5, ALiBi) on Task 1 are not described.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report the same head-wise ablation distributions for all additive baselines on Task 1 so the uniqueness claim is directly supported.

key_concerns.issue: The MLA comparison is not shown to be parameter- or compute-matched, and the claim that the deposit pattern is an 'inefficient use of model capacity' is never measured with any capacity/efficiency metric.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Match parameters/FLOPs between MLA and the standard attention baseline, and either measure capacity utilization directly or soften the inefficiency claim.

key_concerns.issue: Internal inconsistency in the Task 2 narrative: the introduction says RoPE 'underperforms' on the position-agnostic task while Section 4.2 says it 'performs strongly, nearly matching' no-PE methods, yet Table 1 shows RoPE at 69.43 vs. NoPE at 77.69, an 8-point gap.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Reconcile the prose with the numbers and describe RoPE's Task 2 result accurately as a moderate penalty.

key_concerns.issue: Statistical reporting is thin: 'variance less than 5%' over five seeds with no error bars or significance tests in the described results, and the ~60% ablation drop is a single aggregate figure.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report per-seed results, error bars, and a simple significance test for the headline accuracy differences and ablation drops.

questions_for_authors: Is Eq. (2) exact? RoPE applies different rotation angles per frequency pair, so how can the logit matrix be a single Hadamard product with one Toeplitz kernel Ge rather than a sum over per-frequency kernels?
Do additive PEs (Absolute, T5, ALiBi) exhibit any deposit-like concentration on Task 1 under the same head-wise ablation, and where are those violins reported?
Is the deposit head the same head/layer across all five seeds, and how sensitive is the pattern to learning rate, initialization, and model depth?
Is the MLA model parameter- and compute-matched to the RoPE baseline in Table 1?
Can you provide any direct evidence linking the deposit pattern to length-extrapolation failure, even correlational, given that this motivates the paper's central claim?
calibration_check: The limitations section is candid, but the introduction and conclusion still over-scope the evidence by presenting the deposit pattern as the primary cause of RoPE's practical/length-extrapolation gap, a causal link the authors concede is untested.

significance.justification: A mechanistic explanation of RoPE's specialization with an actionable hybrid fix would interest the PE/architecture community, but synthetic-only evidence caps the likely impact.

novelty.justification: The Toeplitz unification is largely a repackaging of known translation-invariance structure, but the deposit-pattern finding and its causal attribution to multiplicative coupling are genuinely new observations.

rigor.justification: The empirical logic is mostly sound, but the theoretical section assumes its key amplification result, proves only an existential cancellation for ALiBi, and uses a questionable single-kernel form of RoPE.

statistical_soundness.justification: Five seeds with reported variance are adequate for toy tasks, but there are no significance tests, no error bars in the described results, and key effects are single aggregate numbers.

calibration_honesty.justification: Limitations are stated, yet the framing overclaims (the deposit pattern as 'primary cause' of RoPE's practical gap) and the Task 2 prose mischaracterizes an 8-point deficit as 'nearly matching'.

clarity.justification: The paper is understandable and logically ordered, but dense run-on prose, typographical artifacts, and occasional internal contradictions impede readability.

structure_compliance.justification: Standard ICLR structure (Introduction, Related Work, Method, Experiments, Ablations, Theory, Conclusion/Limitations) at a reasonable length.

reproducibility.justification: Tasks, dataset sizes, vocabulary, model, and seeds are specified, but hyperparameters, per-head curves, and proofs are deferred to appendices whose content cannot be assessed from the body.

related_work.justification: Coverage of PE variants, NoPE/mechanistic analyses, and Toeplitz spectral theory is broad and reasonably fair, with the contribution delineated in prose.

figure_quality.justification: The captions describe informative, claim-bearing displays (learning curves, head-ablation violins with shape insets, layer-wise p_i ablations, MLA comparison) rather than decoration.

breadth_generality.justification: Two synthetic tasks, one architecture at one scale, no real-data or extrapolation evaluation, and an incompletely supported uniqueness claim fall short of the generality the title and introduction imply.

overall_recommendation.justification: Borderline reject: an interesting, mostly well-executed mechanistic study whose theoretical core and generality claims need substantial additional work before it clears the ICLR bar.
